before: Enacted 2024 as Chapter 238 of the Acts of 2024; codified data-center sales/use tax exemption at G.L. c. 64H Section 6(zz) remains in force as of 2026-07-31
after: Approved in part as Chapter 238 on 2024-11-20; section 214 is listed as effective 2024-11-20, and the published exemption applies to costs incurred after that date (observed 2026-11-07).
rationale: Section 214 amendment-history metadata supplies an effective date; the separate paragraph (zz) note limits applicability to costs incurred after that date. Approval in part is the action, not proof all sections took effect.

before: Creates sales/use tax exemption for qualified data center equipment, software, electricity, and construction costs; 20-year qualification period; 100,000-square-foot and $50 million thresholds.
after: Sales and use tax exemption for eligible equipment, software, electricity and construction costs for qualified data centers; at least 100,000 aggregate square feet, $50 million in qualified costs within 10 years of certification, and at least 100 Massachusetts jobs; facility and building qualification periods are 20 years under specified anchors.
rationale: The original and codified definition specify qualified data center costs and a 100-job requirement; the initial and later building terms have distinct anchors and end-of-calendar-year rules.
The tracked instrument is the enacted statute and codified section, not the underlying proposed bill.
Tax exemption supports an incentive; eligibility conditions do not make its creation an incentive restriction.

Official statute amendment history explicitly dates the section 214 amendment effective November 20, 2024; paragraph (zz) applies to costs incurred after that date, a separate applicability condition.

after: Facility/building-specific 20-year qualification periods, subject to certification and statutory anchors; not a sunset of paragraph (zz).
rationale: The benefit has a specific facility/building qualification endpoint: initial certification and subsequent building commercial operation have different anchors; this does not repeal the exemption itself.
Direct published official codification includes the targeted paragraph.

before: Accompanied a study order (H.5324) 2026-04-06; effectively shelved for the remainder of the 194th General Court
after: Accompanied a study order, H.5324, on 2026-04-06; last action displayed in the official H.4144 history as observed 2026-11-07.
rationale: Study order is the last of five displayed actions; no formal death follows solely from that entry.

before: Broad energy affordability and grid bill; not a data center moratorium bill, but addresses load growth, grid planning, and utility infrastructure cost allocation.
after: Proposes energy affordability and grid measures, including flexible interconnection and stakeholder recommendations on infrastructure financing and customer connections, with data center representatives included.
rationale: Sections 159 and 51 propose flexible connection and stakeholder recommendations; the latter considers financing and avoiding cost shifts, not a finalized cost allocation rule.
Study-order accompaniment alone does not establish failed_died under the codebook.
Planning and flexible interconnection do not impose a construction moratorium; other is the appropriate residual mechanism.
A study order is not proof of a formal failure, enactment, or current operative effect.
Official original-bill history is a direct source.

rationale: Original sections 1 and 3 describe the study drivers and report deadline; the act remains a proposal on the evidence inspected.

before: Would add G.L. c. 164 Section 152 to prevent residential and income-eligible customers from bearing increased electric costs caused by large or qualified data centers; covered facilities include sites able to use 10 MW or more.
after: Would add G.L. c. 164 section 152: distribution companies could not reduce electricity availability or increase rates for residential or income-eligible customers due to covered data centers, defined in part as able to use at least 10 MW; requires departmental rate review and company records.

rationale: New section language protects electricity availability and rates and requires review and records. The 10 MW criterion is ability to use, with parcel and primary-use conditions; it is proposed, not existing law.
